messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert — inference-runtime-prod (us-west-2) high tail latency detected for route `/v1/generate` (model=open-llama-13b). 95th latency > 3s for 5m, error rate spike to 2.1%. Paging on-call.

alex.reed: ack, oncall here. looking now. link to metrics: https://console.redwood.dev/metrics/rt/1768000000 (open in case others want)

deploy-bot: Rollout summary: commit 8f3a2b1 deployed to prod @ 1767999800. Canary -> prod. Changeset highlights: kernel-selection heuristics + kv-cache invalidation enhancement.

maria.kim: seeing OOM-ish growth on kv cache metrics correlated with that commit. KV cache entries exploded for several model shards, causing batching starvation (requests wait while KV WAL grows). this matches the latency pattern.

alex.reed: can we toggle kv cache off as a hotfix rather than full rollback? which is less risk?

maria.kim: toggling KV cache is lower-risk. command to flip: 
```
curl -X POST https://admin-api.us-west-2.redwood/private/runtime/flags -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"kv_cache.enabled": false, "reason": "hotfix - disable until patch"}'
```
will propagate to all runtime nodes in ~30s.

jamie.ops: prepping to run flag change. I'll patch the fleet in the next minute. tagging infra runbook: infra/runbooks/kv-cache-hotfix.md

jamie.ops: running now — patching 24 pods in us-west-2. progress: 6/24

jamie.ops: progress: 12/24

jamie.ops: progress: 24/24 — kv_cache disabled across prod.

incident-bot: kv_cache.enabled=false set fleetwide. New metric check scheduled.

luis.eng: seeing immediate drop in queue depth and 95th latency trending down. good signal.

alex.reed: customer impact check — support, any reports? tina?

tina-support: support queue picked up ~12 customer threads referencing slow responses/timeouts. most are mobile app features experiencing timeouts at ~3–5s. flagged premium accounts: acct-992, acct-211, acct-440. outreach in progress.

sara.product: I'll coordinate customer comms. draft post-incident note in the shared doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/PM-INC-1768000000

ben.sre: running quick health check: memory/heap across runtime nodes. no OOMs seen but memory climbed ~40% on affected shards before kv toggle. need alerting to catch this earlier.

maria.kim: root cause hypothesis: KV cache invalidation path had an edge case when combined with new kernel-selection heuristics and q4f16 quantization profile. results: stale keys persisted and memory accounted incorrectly, causing cache growth and blocking background eviction which in turn prevented efficient batching (batches starved waiting on KV responses).

alex.reed: long-term fixes?

maria.kim: plan: revert incorrect invalidation logic + add stronger invariants + unit + integration tests. also add a canary test that simulates mixed quantization profiles under load.

jamie.ops: ops items: add autoscaling guard rails for memory spikes and configure an alert for kv_cache entry count anomaly. current alert only watches CPU and latency; not kv size.

alex.reed: ok let's capture action items and owners now. I'll spin up a postmortem and set a follow-up meeting.

alex.reed: PM: scheduling postmortem sync Fri 10:00 PST (1768260000). invites to eng-runtime, eng-sre, product, and support. if you can't make it, please add notes to the doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/PM-INC-1768000000

alex.reed: Action items (captured):
- maria.kim: fix kv cache invalidation bug, add unit + integration tests, add canary load test for mixed quant profiles. due: 2 weeks (1769360000).
- jamie.ops: create kv-cache-size alert & autoscale guard for memory spikes, test runbook automation for toggling kv_cache. due: 1 week (1768600000).
- ben.sre: add continuous metric for KV entry growth and tracing hook to link requests to KV ops, update SLO runbook. due: 10 days (1768700000).
- sara.product: prepare customer impact summary and outreach template; coordinate with support on prioritized list. due: 3 days (1768220000).
- luis.eng: add batching regression test and integrate into CI; verify batch_timeout and max_batch_size defaults for q4 quantized models. due: 3 weeks (1769980000).

tina-support: support will send proactive emails to the 12 affected customers today and follow up individually with the premium accounts.

maria.kim: follow-up technical notes: suspected faulty code path sits in runtime/kernel_selector.rs -> invalidate_kv_entries(); will push a draft PR (wip) in next 2 days and link tests. also planning to add metrics: `kv_cache.entry_count` per-shard to reduce MTTR.

jamie.ops: postmortem doc skeleton created and linked in the jira ticket. tagging the oncall handoff: alex.reed -> ben.sre for next 24h monitoring; ben you good to take post-incident watch?

ben.sre: taking handoff. will monitor dashboards and slack alerts. will escalate if any regressions.

alex.reed: thanks everyone. leaving incident channel open until action items start closing. please update the jira/pm doc with progress and ETA changes so we can close the incident formally once all remediation owners mark done. :thumbsup:

maria.kim: quick note — temporary mitigation (kv_cache disabled) may increase token cost; will quantify impact and include in postmortem.

sara.product: noted. adding cost impact section to the PM doc.

jamie.ops: also adding a small automation to auto-disable kv_cache on memory spike > 70% while we patch; temporary but safer than rolling back.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated (kv_cache disabled). severity downgraded to P2 for follow-up.

alex.reed: closing update for now — please log any stray customer reports to the jira linked above. we will reconvene for the postmortem on Fri.

ben.sre: monitoring until 1768080000; will post any anomalies here.
